 Advocate.

Corum: Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, this Court passed the following order: -
(Per : Shri Alok Kumar Verma, J.) This is the Third Bail Application, filed by the appellants Moti Lal, Raju alias Raj Kumar and Makkhan.

2. Appellants have been convicted and sentenced by the learned Special Judge, S.C./S.T. Act,
Dehradun on 15.10.2013 in Special Sessions Trial No.02 of 2013 and as per the order dated 15.10.2013, they have been convicted and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment along with a fine of Rs.5,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(g) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (hereinafter referred to as the "Penal Code") and, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months each, they have been further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years along with a fine of Moti Lal And Two Others ...Appellants vs State Of Uttarakhand on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104303748/
1 Rs.1,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 120B of the Penal Code, and, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months each, they have been further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years along with a fine of Rs.1,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, and, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month each, and, they have been further convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months each for the offence punishable under Section 5/7 of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954.

entities.text: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: All the sentences are directed to run concurrently.
3. The Bail Application of the appellants was rejected by a detailed order dated 30.11.2022.
4. In the present matter, a lady belonging to the weaker section of society was raped by four persons on the pretext of performing some pooja's in an Astrological Center.
5. Once the bail application was rejected, there is no question of granting a similar prayer.
Without the substantial change in the circumstances, successive bail application would be deemed to be seeking review of the earlier order which is not permissible under criminal law.
The appellants had opportunity to raise all their contentions on the previous occasion and they had actually raised the said contentions.
It is not open to the appellants to make successive bail applications even on the grounds already rejected by this Court.
6. Therefore, the present Bail Application does not deserve to be entertained.
Consequently, the present Bail Application is rejected accordingly.
7. In this old Appeal, the appellants can request before the Regular Bench for an early hearing.
